summary.text: Andrew Hevesi is the Democratic incumbent for NY State Assembly District 28 in Queens, first elected in a May 2005 special election. A lifelong resident of the area, he previously worked as a chief of staff and as Director of Community Affairs for the New York City Public Advocate. He chairs the Children and Families Committee and won the June 2026 Democratic primary against Jonathan Rinaldi with 87.7% of the vote.

paragraphs.text: According to his official Assembly biography, he is a lifelong resident of the area he represents, which includes Forest Hills, Rego Park, Ridgewood, Richmond Hill, Middle Village, Glendale and Kew Gardens.
Earned a B.A. in political science from Queens College.
Served as Chief of Staff for Jeff Klein and worked as Director of Community Affairs for the New York City Public Advocate before being elected to the Assembly, according to Ballotpedia.
First elected to the 28th Assembly District on May 10, 2005.
Chaired the Assembly Social Services Committee from 2015 to 2020 and was appointed Chair of the Children and Families Committee in 2021, a post he holds in 2025-2026.
Also serves on the Codes, Health, Rules and Ways and Means committees, the Task Force on New Americans and the Puerto Rican/Hispanic Task Force.

His Assembly biography lists laws he wrote, including a measure prohibiting the arrest and prosecution of children under 12 (excluding homicide), a replacement of anonymous reporting with confidential reporting to the State Central Register of Abuse and Maltreatment, and an extension of the statute of limitations for human-trafficking survivors to bring civil actions.
Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary over Jonathan Rinaldi, 87.7% to 11.8%.
